case_title: CARDINAL MAR GEORGE ALENCHERRY v. STATE OF KERALA & ANR.
neutral_facts: The Syro Malabar Church, an Episcopal Institution, is headed by the appellant-archbishop, who claimed authority over all spiritual and temporal affairs of the church. The appellant allegedly entered into a criminal conspiracy with another accused to fraudulently dispose of certain immovable properties of the church. A complaint was filed against the appellant and others, alleging the commission of offenses under various sections of the IPC. The trial court dismissed the complaint under Section 203 of Cr.P.C. for some offenses but issued summons for others. The appellant and others filed revision applications and petitions under Section 482 Cr.P.C., which were dismissed by the High Court. The Supreme Court held that the trial court's issuance of summons was lawful and that the High Court's subsequent orders exceeded its jurisdiction.
